answer: Churn is counted in hollow, and mirror publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 18% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. An attacker who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the juniper history. A 499 account operation therefore ties up 33 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
